summary: Meningococcal vaccines protect against Neisseria meningitidis serogroups (A and C in the older bivalent polysaccharide product; A, C, W and Y in conjugate vaccines). In India they are used for travellers (including Hajj), outbreaks, asplenia and complement deficiency.
indications: Travel to endemic areas and Hajj

dosage.t: Revaccinate after 3 to 5 years if risk continues

dosage.d: 0.5 mL per product schedule (from 9 months for some)

admin: Use only as the finished product directs
moa: Induces bactericidal anti-capsular antibodies (T-cell dependent for conjugates).
preg: Safety not established; use only if clearly needed
lact: Safety not established; weigh benefit against unknown risk
counsel: Use exactly as the pack directs
Stop and seek care for rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
pearls: Polysaccharide vaccines are poorly immunogenic under 2 years
overdose: No specific antidote. Supportive and symptomatic care.
refs: IAP Advisory Committee on Vaccines and Immunization Practices
World Health Organization: guidelines and position papers
footer: StewardMD-authored DRAFT. No US, Canadian or EU regulatory label exists for this molecule; AI-drafted from the references above and awaiting clinician review. Doses are typical published ranges, not a product label: check the Indian product's own pack insert before prescribing.
